          01. NORTH KAMRUP COLLEGE
                 A PROFILE
P                 North Kamrup College, one of the premier institutions of higher education
          is situated erstwhile in Tribal Sub-Plan area under the traditionally enlightened


R
          Barpeta district of Assam. It was established on the 17th August, 1979.
                  At an early stage of 1978, a team of socially dedicated persons of greater
          Baghmara area felt the need for a higher educational institution for the welfare of
          the society as well as the student community of the greater Baghmara area. Later,

O         with the relentless support of the people with their humble monetary contribution
          and cordiality the institution of higher education named North Kamrup College
          (Arts Stream) came to light in 1979. The College started and grown in a remote rural
          area like Baghmara against many odds like lack of smooth communication as one

S         of them.
                  The College is 13 km. North from Pathsala, of Bajali. Now the International
          Highway No. 127-A from Bhutan to Pathsala is running through Baghmara.


P         Baghmara, where the College is located is a place known for Trade and Business.
          Historically, Baghmara Bazar was famous for exchange of various goods between
          the Assamese and the Bhutanese. People residing in the locality are having diverse
          ethnic identity and colourful cultural heritage. The landscape surrounding the

E         College encovers a spacious campus of 33 Bighas of land covered by boundary
          walls.
                  The founder Principal of this College was Prof. M. M. Datta, a renowned


C
          educationist while veteran Physicist late Dr. P.C. Mahanta (Dean, Faculty of Science,
          GU.) was the first President of the G.B. and late Dr. Ananta Mohan Das, a Physician
          and a social worker of repute had the privilege of leading the institution as the
          Secretary of the public body (G.B). The College vows to attain progress and run

T         ahead in the days to come with the unsparing support of the students, the guardians,
          the society by and large and the alumni as it is launched and meant for attainment
          of excellence in higher education. Since its inception, this institution has been playing
          a significant role in the socio-cultural and literary field of Assam. Today it has

U         emerged as a leading College in Assam by keeping pace with the changing world.
                  The College campus bears a large number of valuable trees and in
          collaboration with the Department of Social Forestry, Govt. of Assam, seedlings of


S         valuable trees like Saal, Nahar, Teak, Sishu, Gameri etc. are being produced in 5
          Bighas of college land which are likely to help in creating environmental awareness
          among the students.

            1) The academic work in each semester will require the student to engage with

                Every course will have defined learning objectives and may be designed to

                academic requirement of the course as per the Affiliating University. .
            3) An undergraduate degree programme with Honours in a discipline will have
                a course credit requirement of 148 credits while an undergraduate degree


C               program without Honours will require a student to earn 132 course credits.
                Students in an Honours programme can opt to earn additional credits by

                consideration in computation of the student’s grade but will be recorded in
                the grade sheet.

          03.242 Elective Course: An Elective course is to be chosen by the student from a

P                pool of such courses on offer and will essentially be of three types:

S             b) Generic Elective Course: A Generic Elective Course is offered by an

                 programme with Honours can acquire 24 course credits from Generic

          enshrined in our Constitution- a democratic, just, socially conscious, cultured and
          humane nation upholding liberty, equality, fraternity and justice for all. The new


O
          policy therefore attempts to synthesize and harmonize the knowledge of ancient
          India and the emerging knowledge of the different fields so that the education system
          produces world leaders in all fields of human endeavour. The system wants to do
          away with rote learning and encourage critical thinking, logical decision making

S         and innovation. It wants to reestablish India once again as world or global teacher
          (vishwaguru) across all fields of knowledge as it once was in the ancient time. The
          FYUGP is designed to fulfill the diverse academic needs of the student and seeks


P         to offer options of multiple entries/exits and obtain a Certificate or a Diploma or
          Degree with Major or a Degree (Honours) or a Degree (Honours) with Research at
          various levels as stipulated under the policy.

                 India and promote local language and knowledge through the various stages
                 in the curriculum.
